questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Planner 1's memo proposes higher government spending and lower taxes; what stance is this?

options.text: Expansionary fiscal policy that shifts aggregate demand right
Contractionary fiscal policy that shifts aggregate demand left
Neutral fiscal policy with no demand effect
Monetary policy acting through interest rates

questions.explanation: Higher spending and lower taxes increase aggregate demand. This is expansionary fiscal policy, shifting AD to the right.
questions.hint: More spending or lower taxes is expansionary.

questions.stem: Planner 3's memo notes rising consumer confidence; explain the AD effect.

questions.explanation: Consumer confidence affects consumption, a direct component of AD. Higher confidence raises spending and shifts AD right.
questions.hint: Consumption is part of aggregate demand.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Planner 4's memo assumes MPC of 0.80; what is the spending multiplier?
questions.explanation: Spending multiplier equals 1/(1-MPC). With MPC 0.80, denominator is 0.20, so multiplier is 5.
questions.hint: Divide 1 by one minus MPC.

questions.explanation: Tax multiplier equals -MPC/(1-MPC). With MPC 0.80, it is -0.8/0.2 or -4. Tax cuts raise GDP, but by less than spending increases.
questions.hint: Tax multiplier is negative MPC over one minus MPC.
